## Rule Description

Describe the proposed chemical rule, the functional group or molecular motif it targets, and why the rule should be introduced or modified in MolSanitizer.

## Relevant Component(s)

Select all that apply.

- [ ] Neutralizer
- [ ] Ionizer
- [ ] Tautomerizer

## Proposed SMARTS Rule (Optional)

Provide the proposed SMARTS pattern or transformation rule, if available. If the suggestion concerns an existing rule, specify which rule should be modified or replaced.

## Example Compounds (Required)

Provide at least **two representative compounds** supporting the proposed rule. Each example should include:

- Compound name and SMILES.
- Expected protonation state, neutral form, or dominant tautomer.
- Relevant pKa value(s) and/or evidence of the dominant molecular form in an aqueous solution or protein-binding site environment.
- Relevant experimental conditions (e.g., pH, solvent, or protein-binding environment), if available.

| Compound | SMILES | pKa (if applicable) | Expected molecular form | Reference |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Compound 1 | | | | |
| Compound 2 | | | | |

## Supporting References (Required)

Provide scientific references supporting the proposed rule and the expected molecular forms of the example compounds.

**Experimental evidence is strongly preferred** over computational predictions. Relevant sources may include:

- Experimentally determined pKa values.
- Experimental studies of tautomeric or protonation equilibria.
- Spectroscopic evidence (e.g., NMR or UV–Vis).
- Structural or spectroscopic studies supporting the assigned molecular form in protein-binding sites.
- Peer-reviewed scientific publications and curated experimental databases.

Please provide DOIs, URLs, or database identifiers wherever possible. Clearly distinguish experimental evidence from computational predictions.

## Scope and Exceptions (Optional)

Describe any known exceptions, substituent effects, or chemical environments in which the proposed rule may not be applicable.

## Additional Context (Optional)

Provide any additional information, chemical structures, figures, or supporting materials that may help us evaluate and validate the proposed rule.
